title: Constitutional adequacy of notice
summary: Notice is the communication needed to give an affected person a meaningful opportunity to protect an interest before a court acts. Mullane evaluates whether the method is reasonably calculated, under the circumstances, to inform interested persons.
notes: Due process ordinarily asks for a reasonable method rather than a guarantee of actual receipt. Compliance with a service rule and constitutional adequacy are separate inquiries.

sections.Meaning: Notice is the communication needed to give an affected person a meaningful opportunity to protect an interest before a court acts. Mullane evaluates whether the method is reasonably calculated, under the circumstances, to inform interested persons.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the interests affected, what addresses or other contact information are known or reasonably available, the proposed method, and any reason to know it failed. Distinguish readily identifiable people from unknown or unlocatable persons.
